name: SWE-eval (Deng et al.)
date_note: The dated name-map check records the public protocol; this is not a release date.
input: An issue and the agent’s recorded steps
output: A patch and the trajectory that produced it
assessment: Compare resource use, consistency and information gained from tools alongside issue resolution.
description: Evaluate how a coding agent reaches its answer, not just whether the final patch passes.

name: SweEval (language use)
input: A writing request with a specified tone and context
assessment: Check whether the response includes the requested profanity across contexts and languages.
description: Study how language models handle requests to use profanity in everyday writing.

name: CWEval
input: A programming task specification
assessment: Check functional behavior and security separately; passing functional tests does not establish security.
description: The authors test functional correctness and security in generated code. Distinct from CWE-bench.

name: AgentEval (AgentGym)
input: An instruction and observations from the environment
assessment: Evaluate success under each environment’s task rules.
description: AgentEval is the benchmark suite inside AgentGym. Both names lead to this same evaluation.

name: AgentExam
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: A repository issue in a prepared workspace
output: An attempted fix and a recorded run
assessment: The project’s deterministic grader reports whether the issue was resolved.
description: An implemented coding-agent evaluation protocol records runs and resolved task outcomes; not SCI-AGENT-EXAM.

name: AgentDojo
input: A user task and tool responses
output: The assistant’s actions and final state
assessment: Report task utility and security outcomes separately.
description: The authors evaluate tool-using assistants on utility and security tasks.

name: agent squared
date_note: The dated name-map check records the public protocol; this is not a release date.
input: A market or negotiation scenario
assessment: The project reports separate negotiation, rationality, robustness and stability scores.
description: This suite reports controlled trading and negotiation tests for AI agents. “Squared” is part of its name.

name: ToolGym
input: A task with constraints and an available tool set
assessment: The environment checks task outcomes and adherence to constraints.
description: The first paper uses ToolGym for a tool-use evaluation with verifiable rewards. Later versions are titled C-World.

name: Reasoning-Bench (Inspect)
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: A question from the selected task
assessment: Use the scorer for that task; this implementation does not define a new common test set.
description: This exact-named suite implements existing reasoning tasks in Inspect with runnable evaluations; it is not a new underlying dataset.

name: ReasoningEval
input: A problem and the model’s reasoning steps
output: A reasoning trace and its final answer
assessment: The Knowledge Index and Information Gain distinguish different contributions of individual steps.
description: The authors’ evaluation framework scores reasoning steps with Knowledge Index and Information Gain.

name: Reasoning Gym
input: A generated puzzle with configurable difficulty
output: A proposed solution to the puzzle
assessment: Each generator supplies its own answer checker or partial-credit scoring rule.
description: Procedural reasoning tasks have verifiable answers and task-specific scoring.

name: MM-Eval (model judges)
input: A multilingual task and candidate responses
assessment: Compare model judgments with the reference judgments across languages and task categories.
description: Test whether a model can evaluate answers in different languages. MM here does not mean multimodal.

name: MM-Eval (Modern Mongolian)
input: A Mongolian syntax, semantics, knowledge or reasoning question
output: An answer in the task’s requested format
assessment: Report correctness by skill rather than treating this as a multilingual judge benchmark.
description: Answer Modern Mongolian questions ranging from syntax to mathematical reasoning.

name: VisionBench (EuroSAT)
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: A EuroSAT RGB satellite image
assessment: Compare balanced accuracy and macro F1 on the frozen test split across seeds.
description: The project ships a frozen EuroSAT evaluation: five classifiers, three seeds and a preregistered held-out test protocol. It is distinct from the OpenCV development tool.

name: VisionEval
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: Images from the project’s test manifest
assessment: Compare with expected results and a saved baseline; track previously failed cases.
description: This project ships sample manifests, a baseline comparison and a scored visual regression suite; it is not the transport-planning project.

name: Video-Bench (generation)
input: A text prompt for the generator
assessment: Evaluate visual quality and alignment with the prompt across the project’s dimensions.
description: Test generated video against a prompt suite. The 2023 understanding benchmark is a separate project.

name: Video-Bench (understanding)
input: A video and a question about it
assessment: Evaluate answers across the underlying video-understanding tasks.
description: The 2023 project tests whether a model understands existing videos rather than generating new ones.

name: VideoEval
input: Video clips from the selected downstream task
assessment: VidTAB measures few-shot adaptation; VidEB tests the usefulness of video embeddings.
description: VideoEval scores video foundation models on a low-cost suite of vision tasks.

name: VideoGym
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: An initial task image and instructions
assessment: Verifiers check the generated video across held-out tasks and difficulty levels.
description: VideoGym ships a seven-level evaluation with held-out tasks, seeds and verifiers, alongside its training code.

name: video-rsi
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: A generated clip with its audio
assessment: Report separate checks, including dialogue and motion; a skipped check is not a pass.
description: This suite scores generated clips with audio and video checks. Separately, the Video-RSI paper describes a learning method.

name: EmbodiedEval
input: An instruction and views of a simulated environment
output: Actions or answers grounded in the scene
assessment: Evaluate task completion in the interactive environment.
description: The project evaluates multimodal models with embodied-agent tasks.

name: Embodied First Exam
input: A task and observations permitted by the setting
output: Control actions or a program that controls the robot
assessment: Compare task success within the same observation, timing and reset conditions.
description: The paper presents a benchmark for coding agents performing physically grounded tasks.

name: RoboBench (Luo et al.)
input: A question about a robot scene and visual evidence
assessment: Score multiple-choice responses and plans under their respective protocols.
description: Test a multimodal model’s understanding and planning for robot scenes, not direct motor control.

name: Robo-bench (Vals AI)
input: A written task, camera images and robot sensor readings
output: Motor commands during a timed episode
assessment: Vals AI checks progress on its simulated arm and humanoid tasks; most tasks are held out.
description: Control a robot through its sensors and motors in a physics simulator.

name: RoboEval
input: Camera observations and robot state
assessment: Report completion alongside stage progress, coordination and movement quality.
description: A bimanual manipulation benchmark with task families and published success and diagnostic metrics.

name: RoboGym (carlo-scr)
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: Image or state observations from a manipulation episode
output: Robot actions before and after a change of conditions
assessment: Compare success and recovery under paired changes to the scene or physics.
description: This RoboGym includes a manipulation benchmark protocol with fixed tasks, shifts and recovery metrics. It is distinct from OpenAI’s same-named simulation framework.

name: Robots’ Last Exam
input: A work request and observations from the scene
output: A completed physical workflow in simulation
assessment: Check the final deliverable and required intermediate conditions; report subtask success separately.
description: Carry out a complete workplace request, such as preparing an order in a simulated beverage shop.

name: AlignmentBench (Brida AI)
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: A scenario and its governing policy
assessment: Evaluate behavior against the stated policy boundaries rather than a universal alignment score.
description: The project evaluates model and agent actions against explicit policies. The similar name AlignBench belongs to a different benchmark.

name: alignment_eval
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: A fixed set of prompts
output: A model response to each prompt
assessment: The project classifies responses as refusals or approvals.
description: This runnable model evaluation applies fixed inputs and classifies responses as refusal or approval. The repository uses an underscore.

name: Alignment Gym (FluffAI)
input: Personality questionnaire items under a language and persona condition
output: A response to each questionnaire item
assessment: Score questionnaire traits and compare profiles across order, language and persona conditions.
description: The authors call the evaluation “Alignment Gym” and specify language, persona, item-order and model-scoring conditions for their psychometrics track.

name: LongEval (long-text generation)
input: A long-form writing request
output: A directly generated or planned long text
assessment: Evaluate length and content quality, comparing direct and plan-based writing.
description: Measure how well a model sustains content across a long answer.

name: LongEval (CLEF 2023 retrieval)
input: Search topics and document collections from different time periods
output: A ranking of documents for each topic
assessment: Compare retrieval effectiveness against relevance judgments across time periods.
description: The CLEF 2023 retrieval track tests whether a search system remains useful as web content changes.

name: MemoryBench (THUIR)
input: A sequence of text tasks with feedback
assessment: Compare downstream task metrics with and without accumulated experience.
description: The authors benchmark memory and continuous learning in large language models.

name: memory-eval (wyyyyn)
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: Conversation history and later queries
assessment: Compare the architectures by dimension, including retrieval relevance and capacity degradation.
description: This suite compares four conversational memory architectures across seven dimensions; the repository identifier matches exactly.

name: MemoryDojo
input: Tasks spanning multiple sessions
assessment: Compare task utility and memory safety outcomes under the paper’s conditions.
description: The paper explicitly names MemoryDojo and evaluates the effects of poisoned information on agent memory.

name: Memory Gym
input: A sequence of local visual observations
assessment: Compare episode rewards and performance as the demand on memory increases.
description: Procedurally generated partially observable tasks evaluate memory-dependent agent behavior.

name: ResearchBench (ResearchTown)
input: A research-community graph with a masked paper or review component
output: A predicted piece of research writing
assessment: Compare predicted text with the held-out content using similarity measures.
description: The ResearchTown authors explicitly name this dataset for paper-writing and peer-review tasks ResearchBench.

name: research-eval (Gimbal v0.19.4)
input: Fixed questions and a local source collection
assessment: The versioned Gimbal workflow evaluates outputs against its fixed source-based tasks.
description: Gimbal’s named evaluation compares research and indexing models on fixed local-source tasks with independent assessment; it is a component, not a standalone paper.

name: ResearchGym
input: A research repository with data, baselines and an evaluator
assessment: Compare with the provided baselines on each paper’s own metric.
description: The paper explicitly introduces ResearchGym for evaluating language-model agents doing AI research.

name: Scientists’ First Exam
input: A scientific visual and a question
output: An answer grounded in the visual evidence
assessment: Measure question accuracy across perception, understanding and reasoning.
description: The paper uses this exact name for a multimodal scientific cognition benchmark.

name: Life-Bench (multimodal personalization)
input: Visual and textual context about a fictional person
assessment: Evaluate whether the response uses the supplied personal knowledge correctly.
description: Use knowledge of a person’s life to answer personalized questions about images.

name: LIFEBench (length instructions)
input: A prompt with a requested response length
output: A generated text of the requested size
assessment: Compare the actual length with the instruction over different target lengths.
description: Test whether a model follows explicit length requirements when writing.

name: LifeBench (multi-source memory)
input: A user’s simulated digital traces and a later question
output: An answer combining evidence across time and sources
assessment: Check answers against references for facts, events, habits and procedures.
description: Recover information about a simulated life from events distributed over many sources.

name: LifeGym v26.8.12
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: A simulated life scenario, messages and service observations
output: Decisions and changes to the simulated services
assessment: Weighted checks assess individual stages, cross-stage dependencies and the final state.
description: The LifeGym reference suite defines a 200-task evaluation for long-horizon agents with weighted stage and final checks. It is separate from VibeLifeBench.

name: FrontierEval (review study)
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: The same set of pull requests under two review conditions
assessment: Compare which known issues were found with and without the plugin.
description: Repeatable coding-agent evaluation: score known issues found in the same 15 pull requests with and without the review plugin. The programs and review results are public.

name: Humanity’s First Exam (pilot)
input: Questions with historically documented positions
output: The model’s position or its account of historical views
assessment: Compare answers against the same source-backed position key under both question types.
description: Six-question pilot with a historical position key. The protocol compares model responses and their reports of historical arguments against the same reference positions.

name: metabench (sparse reasoning and knowledge)
input: A selected subset of knowledge and reasoning items
output: Model answers to the selected items
assessment: Estimate performance using a small item set selected for its statistical information.
description: Use a smaller, statistically selected test set to measure language-model ability.

name: MetaBench (metabolomics)
input: Questions about metabolomics concepts and their relationships
output: An answer to each scientific question
assessment: Evaluate performance on the named domain tasks, not on general reasoning items.
description: Test domain knowledge and reasoning about metabolomics.

name: MetaEval (Wang et al.)
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: Model predictions on benchmark questions
assessment: Assess how well individual items distinguish the tested models.
description: The authors evaluate how well benchmark items discriminate between LLMs. Not just the generic term meta-evaluation.

name: MetaGym (PaddlePaddle)
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: Task-specific observations from the selected environment
output: A policy’s actions over an episode
assessment: Use the reward and termination rules of each environment; there is no single suite-wide score.
description: PaddlePaddle’s named RL benchmarking suite includes task generators with specified observations, rewards, and termination (e.g. MetaMaze). Not the unrelated agent-training library of the same name.

name: BenchBench (generation)
input: A task specification derived from a seed benchmark
assessment: Grade model answers to the new items and check item validity and discrimination.
description: Evaluate models as authors of benchmark items rather than only as test takers.

name: BenchBench leaderboard (agreement)
input: Model performance measurements from multiple benchmarks
output: Agreement statistics for the compared evaluations
assessment: Compare rankings with explicit choices of models, peer benchmarks and agreement metric.
description: The BenchBench package and its leaderboard test agreement among evaluation results.

name: Benchmark²
task: Quality of benchmark items and rankings
input: Model results on multiple benchmarks
assessment: Measure ranking consistency, model discrimination and deviations from expected capability ordering.
description: The authors write Benchmark^2 and apply a named protocol to evaluate LLM benchmarks. The exponent is part of the name.

name: BenchBenchBench
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: Frozen submissions from benchmark designers and independent test evidence
output: A comparison of selected designers on held-out cases
assessment: Check whether a public selection score identifies authors that perform well independently.
description: Named holdout audit: tests whether benchmark-generation evaluators select authors that succeed on independent evidence.

name: ResearchArena (AI R&D oversight)
input: A research task and outputs submitted for review
output: Research work and a monitor’s assessment
assessment: Report useful task performance alongside the monitor’s ability to identify compromised work.
description: Evaluate oversight of automated AI research, not literature search or survey writing.

name: GameEval
input: A game role, objective and dialogue history
assessment: Each game’s rules score whether the assigned objective is achieved.
description: Game-playing: models converse to achieve objectives in dialogue games. The benchmark evaluates their play, not games they generate.

name: GameDojo
input: Game observations during a boss encounter
assessment: Evaluate progress and encounter outcomes under the specified interaction setting.
description: Game-playing: interactive agents fight bosses in existing video games. The suite contains 120 encounters across 20 games.

name: Game Gym (nunu.ai)
input: A task and the agent’s view of the game
assessment: Use the task-specific outcomes defined by the game environment.
description: Game-playing: nunu.ai measures agents on tasks in 3D games, with scoring specific to each game. Not a game engine or a creation contest.

name: GameArena (Hu et al.)
input: A game state and exchanges with a human player
assessment: Game-specific measures separate reasoning skills using the recorded sessions.
description: People play reasoning games with language models; this is not Kaggle’s model-versus-model track.

name: Game Arena (LLM Stats)
date_note: The dated name-map check records the public protocol; this is not a release date.
input: A prompt describing a game to build
output: A playable game generated by a model
assessment: The track uses community comparisons. The site has stopped accepting new Arena submissions.
description: The LLM Stats coding track compares games that models make, not how well the models play.

name: HarnessBench (reacher-z)
date_note: This dated project revision documents the evaluation; it need not be the first release.
input: An everyday task with access to online services
output: Work completed through the chosen harness
assessment: Compare task outcomes across harnesses while holding the model fixed.
description: Use the same model to compare harnesses on everyday online work; this is separate from Qihoo360’s Harness-Bench.
